hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I'm here to help you through the Child Benefit eligibility assessment. To get started, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is the child you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please tell me:
- The child's name (or names if you have multiple children)
- Each child's age or date of birth

This will help me determine which eligibility path applies to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 6 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're asking about **Alex, who is 6 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, this is great news - he automatically qualifies as a qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes. Let me continue through the assessment to check the other eligibility requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check a few more things about Alex's situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(Note: This is typically not an issue for 6-year-olds, but I need to ask to complete the full assessment)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 6!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes sense - he's just 6 years old. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(Again, this is typically not the case for a 6-year-old, but I need to check for completeness)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

For a 6-year-old, the answer should be no, but I need to ask to be thorough with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not - he's only 6!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency situation. This is important for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do any of the following apply to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common situation)

2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**

3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme AND:**
   - You're working and earning/expect to earn above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months, OR
   - You're actively seeking work (as a jobseeker for up to 91 days), OR
   - You have sufficient resources to support yourself and family financially and are NOT claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit, OR
   - You're studying and have sufficient resources, OR
   - You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside

4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad or in certain qualifying countries**

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I don't live in the UK at the moment - I'm living abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see - thank you for clarifying that. Let me ask a few more questions to understand your situation better.

**Can you tell me:**

1. **Are you a Crown servant?** (For example, working for the UK government, armed forces, or in a diplomatic role abroad)

2. **If not a Crown servant, do you have any status under the EU Settlement Scheme?** (Settled status, pre-settled status, or neither)

3. **Which country are you currently living in?**

This will help me determine if you still qualify for Child Benefit under the special circumstances for people living abroad.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I don't have any EU settlement status either. I'm just living abroad with my family at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Unfortunately, based on the information you've provided, it appears you may not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit.

The rules state that to be eligible for Child Benefit, you normally need to:
- Live in the UK, OR
- Have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, OR
- Meet one of the other special circumstances (such as being a Crown servant abroad)

Since you're living abroad without any of these special statuses, you wouldn't qualify for Child Benefit at this time.

However, before I give you the final outcome, let me check one important thing:

**Are you planning to return to the UK soon, or is this a temporary arrangement?** 

Also, **is there any possibility you might qualify under any of the other circumstances I mentioned** - for example, are you working and earning above the National Insurance threshold, or do you have sufficient resources?

This will help me ensure I'm giving you the most accurate assessment of your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we're settled here for now - it's not just a temporary thing. And no, none of those other circumstances apply to me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Based on the residency requirements for Child Benefit, I need to give you the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me provide you with the formal outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Final Outcome: **INELIGIBLE**

**For Alex (age 6):**
Unfortunately, you are not eligible for Child Benefit at this time because you do not meet the residency requirements.

**Why:**
- While Alex meets the age requirement (under 16), Child Benefit requires the claimant to normally live in the UK
- You are currently living abroad and do not have any of the qualifying statuses that would allow you to claim while abroad (such as settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme or Crown servant status)

**What this means:**
You cannot claim Child Benefit while you're living abroad in your current circumstances.

**Next steps:**
- If you return to the UK in the future, you would be able to apply for Child Benefit at that time
- You can contact HMRC for more information about whether any other circumstances might apply to your situation
- For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if you return to the UK), please feel free to come back and we can reassess your eligibility.
